venues.name: CC Atlanta
venues.narrative:
**CCATL — Thursday, July 16, 2026** (MOD: MKZ // JK, entered by JK)

Very chill Thursday at CC ATL tonight. 8 Meal Deals in total to start us off.

Weather was gloomy in our area for long periods of time as it was storming pretty heavily in other areas around Atlanta during the early evening hours.

It stayed quiet till about 11pm when we got a small pop of folks coming in for a few late-night cocktails.

Barback was on to work on prep as we head into the weekend. Acid Celery Cordial batch was finished from our previous prep session and another started. Barback stayed to close the bar as support.

Smooth end to the night with everyone out of our space by 12am. Opener was cut at 7pm.

**Comps:** Industry Love $6.50, O4W $2.20 — total $8.70.

**Kitchen:** Hot Dog ABK — looking for a diagonal paper placement in a diamond orientation, corner points landing at the ends of the basket. The loaded dog will now be topped with 3-4 banana peppers for acidity. Ketchup and mustard now go on top of the relish on the Classic Dog.

**Favorite moment:** Seeing Raven from Casi Cielo — a great regular who is always sending folks down the stairs to visit our space.

venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.weather: Hot and humid with brief rain
venues.narrative:
**CCNSH — Thursday, July 16, 2026** (MOD & Chef: KK/KE & JMS, entered by JO)

Had ourselves a nice Thursday night! Slow start to service with only doing about $700 in sales, but we picked right up around 8:45pm and kept consistently busy until 11pm. Most of our sales were made from 9pm - 10:30pm which means we were slingin' some drinks. Separate from our 20 top res we had another birthday party of a 30-40 person walk-in. It felt very much like a weekend night in here at one point.

**Comps:** $43.50 / 1.4%.

**Kitchen:** Decent food sales, we would always like to see more! John-Michael held it down in the kitchen and helping us out in front as well.

**Events:** Our 20 top res had themselves a great time.

**Favorite moment:** Rockin' service with Brandon C and Sara! We were definitely feeling it at one point while the rush was pouring in, but we kept our cool and ended having a fun night.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative:
**DVR — Thursday, July 16, 2026** (AM MOD: Maggie & Chef Lucas; PM MOD: Evan)

**Sales split:** DC/AM $1,356.13 | D&C (PM) $10,838.83 | Garden/6A $3,482.43. Total net $12,194.96 vs target $11,421 (+6.8%). Comps $252.55 (~2.07%). 226 guests (Tock).

**D&C Notes:** Overall a great night! Garden was cruising but never out of hand; steady people moving through the lobby. Everyone was on the ball. Great sales, low comps, happy people!

**DC/AM Notes:** Thursday was a quick day. Lots of food, cocktails and coffee most of the day. There's a fresh batch of citrus green iced tea. Coffee order came today. We did run out of tortillas but they are back in stock now. -Reggie

**Garden / 6A:** STEAAAAADY day in the heat but we made money and had fun. - Dom

**Kitchen:** Great and chill night with Chef Lucas, Rand and Marv!! -Rachel

**Maintenance:** Ticket rail on B500 fell off again.

**Favorite moment:** Getting a lot of meetings done and checking things off with MS ||| Watching Ryan S killin' it on the floor ||| Having the garden be busy and bumpin' but not chaotic.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.narrative:
**EV — Thursday, July 16, 2026** (MOD & Chef: Kyler and Steves, entered by stef)

**Service Notes:** A busy Thursday that kept the room turning with only a few lulls in service. We welcomed in many first timers as well as many investors looking to show off our bar for their dates/groups. With DK at the bar and a steady flow of mid sized tops, we kept the room lively and energetic through the slower parts. We ended the night with some people who maybe had a bit too much, but no big issues arose and we were able to get everyone out happy.

**Top sellers:** Rosalie, Crowd Work, Native Lion and Crossover Episode tied.

**Door Notes:** Tonight's weather transported us to a scene from Dune or Blade Runner 2049, an orange sun and much more smoke and smog filling the city. However it still didn't stop many New Yorkers from venturing out for a drink with friends. We welcomed a ton of birthdays, many being large parties, who all had an incredible time!

At 6pm we got about half full, and a huge 8pm turn (36 covers in 30 min) creating a little lull for space, but after 8pm we kept relatively full until 11pm, after then slowing down for the night. All 11:45pm reservations came early, most folks heading home early, and the bar became mostly empty with larger parties holding on until 1:30am.

Special guests included David Kaplan to the bar with friends, Marisela (past EV bartender), Raymond (friend of Elis's daughter), Milos from Kafana in for his birthday, Ben Hood (past server at Mace), and Sara in again with a bunch of the Batemans crew. Also devoted regular Saju, and members Eric Poon and Ezra Ende celebrating his fiancée's birthday. No no-shows.

**Glassware breakage:** champagne flute, SOF, footed pilsner, candle votive.

**Maintenance:** Paneling beneath sink in front of bathroom upstairs needs to be reattached.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.narrative:
**LA — Thursday, July 16, 2026** (MOD & Chef: Gigi & Josh/Oscar, entered by Gigi)

**D&C Notes:** Busy, busy, busy! A nice steady start, and at 8pm we kicked into high gear until 11pm. As soon as Julian got here, he already had plenty of tables in his section. We did have a party of 14 that took over tables 24 and 25 and stayed the entire night. Plenty of walk-ins to fill the entire room, and lots of large party walk-ins and reservations to fill up tables 1-3. Streets were busy all night. Natalie hustled to seat every party! We had a short waitlist and we were able to get almost everyone in, with the exception of a few large groups. We cut Edwin around 11:30pm and Bailey around 12am. Ryan did a great job barbacking tonight! We had some really sweet people in the building tonight, and huge shout out to the whole team for giving them exceptional service!

**Kitchen:** People were ordering oysters by the dozen! So many french fries and steak tartares — very busy night for food and looking forward to a busy weekend ahead! Oscar and Josh did an amazing job!

**Comps:** $183.51 — Ray, Jorge with Perra Suerte + friends visiting from Guadalajara, birthdays, anniversaries, Angel, Julian staff food.

**Maintenance:** Critters in the SR.

**Favorite moment:** Jorge from Perra Suerte having a mini tasting of their Raicilla with the team — we got to try 2 different ones! Salud!

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.narrative:
**DC — Thursday, July 16, 2026** (MOD: Marcus)

**D&C Notes:** It was a hot one tonight, and the outdoor air quality declined as the evening went on. Despite that, the Toast transition continues to move in the right direction. We had a solid opening rush that tapered off around 8:15pm, followed by a smaller pop around 10:00pm. We finished the night with a few tables, some solo bar guests, and an 8-top that arrived around 11:00pm.

A little industry support to kick off the shift! Raleigh and Amber stopped by and are planning to visit D&C East Village tomorrow. If they can't make it, they have a reservation with us at 6:00pm on Monday. Tyler and Mariah handled the opening rush really well, with the bar team stepping out to support the floor at the peak of service.

**Guests:** 82 total — 27 reservations, 55 walk-ins.

**Toast/KDS Notes:** A few 'missing tickets' on the bar KDS were actually being routed to the Garden — use the search function to see whether each item is designated for Marquee or Garden in the item description. On both kitchen and bar KDS you can complete individual items on a ticket without completing the entire order (tap the ticket once to open the item list). Handhelds are assigned to specific locations and labeled accordingly — please keep them in their designated areas.

The Hoshizaki ice machine was repaired this afternoon. Amazonia helped us out with a couple of buckets to get us started while the machine caught up. It's now running well and the pooling issue has been resolved.

Last call came naturally at 12:30, but we still had campers up till close.

**Kitchen:** Awesome first night for Maria in the kitchen! James and Maria had a nice pop at the start of shift, but it died down the same time as the room. It did allow them time to go through the menu and some prep. Loved the energy on the line tonight!

**Comps:** Total $99.22 — Industry $13.90, Community/investor $4.32, Spill $22, Service recovery $26, Gift $10, DNL $23.

**What we can do better:** Bar reminders — use all equipment for its intended purpose; always pour liquids over the scupper; ice glassware while it's resting on the scupper, never while holding it over the ice well.

**Maintenance:** Curtains coming off rails; lightbulb in party pod; lightbulbs in garden.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.narrative:
**MG — Thursday, July 16, 2026** (AM MOD: Sam & Lex/Shannon; PM MOD: Justin / Shannon & Drew; entered by Alexis)

**Sales split:** Municipal Bar AM $848 | Municipal Bar PM $3,358 | Sun Club $533 | Hot Eye $1,386. Total net $8,626 vs target $6,000 (+43.8%). Guest counts (OpenTable): 26 AM, 70 PM.

**Morning MB:** A very quiet morning. Our busiest hour was noon-1 with a 20 person food tour. Most of them got drinks to go so that was a big help. Eva and Sierra knocked it all out no problem. The kitchen had no problem with their food ticket as usual and they were kind enough to make extra of the new food items so the AM servers not in the meeting could taste. An easy day.

**Evening MB:** Another very slow and steady night for MB, slower than a typical Thursday. Did not jump up too far from existing covers. Bar never filled up, and a max 7 tables in the dining room at our peak hour of 8:30. Things before and after were pretty quiet. A few walk-ins for drinks after kitchen closing, with many parties opting to go downstairs!

**Sun Club:** Pretty good crowd throughout the day, all familiar faces staying in the hotel. A storm came in late afternoon, and even though it was pouring down, four people came up and sat under the roof of the bar the whole time. Super chill day but lots of drinkers!

**Hot Eye:** We had a very slow, but steady start to the night with a handful of hotel guests and tourists. By 10pm the room did a 180 with very LARGE parties walking in all at the same time. Sam and I got swamped for a second but handled the volume well. We stayed busy till close with our normal service industry crowd, our very own James, and late night hotel guests. Energy was good tonight, along with some great conversations with guests!

**Kitchen:** Gelato will be back tomorrow, as well as our new menu going LIVE!

**Events:** No event; $2,315 in sales captured today from a previous event (June 9th).

**Favorite moment:** The FOH staff getting together to taste the new food items — brunch is about to be a big hit!
